kana.title: Master kana first
kana.body: Hiragana and Katakana are the foundation of everything. Spend a few days until you can read them without romaji.

short.title: A little, every day
short.body: 15 minutes daily beats 3 hours once a week. Protect your streak to build the habit.

spaced.title: Review before you forget
spaced.body: New words fade fastest within 1–2 days. Review vocabulary regularly to move it into long-term memory.

kanji.title: Learn kanji in context
kanji.body: Don't memorize kanji in isolation. Learn them with the words that use them, and follow the correct stroke order.

write.title: Write by hand
write.body: Writing answers yourself makes your brain work harder than picking an option, so words last longer.

listen.title: Train your ear
listen.body: Replay the audio many times, even casually. Listening only improves with exposure.

speak.title: Say it out loud
speak.body: Speaking aloud trains your tongue and your ear at once. Repeat conversation scenarios until you can do them without looking at the text.

quiz.title: Test after you study
quiz.body: Right after finishing a lesson, do its practice questions. Recalling beats re-reading.

dashboard.tip_jlpt_sub: Practical steps, straight to the features that help.

format.title: Know the exam format
format.body: JLPT has Moji-Goi, Bunpou-Dokkai, and Chokai sections. Take one full test to learn the question types and pacing.

vocab.title: Strengthen vocabulary & kanji
vocab.body: Most questions test vocabulary and kanji. Review regularly until words are mastered, then check frequent kanji.

grammar.title: Understand grammar patterns
grammar.body: Memorize sentence patterns with their examples. Use the reference when unsure, and don't just memorize meanings.

listening.title: Train listening daily
listening.body: The Chokai section often decides pass or fail. Start with short audio, then move to longer conversations.

time.title: Practice time management
time.body: Take tests in strict mode with the timer to get used to it. Skip stuck questions and return at the end.

review.title: Learn from your mistakes
review.body: After a test, open the review and note your error patterns. That's where your score improves fastest.

final_week.title: Tidy up the final week
final_week.body: Review weak material, do not start new topics the day before, sleep well, and never leave an answer blank on exam day.

kana.title: Hiragana & Katakana
kana.dakuten_intro: Dakuten (゛), or "tenten", is a two-stroke mark at the upper right of a character. It turns a voiceless consonant sound into a voiced one: k→g, s→z, t→d, h→b.
kana.handakuten_intro: Handakuten (゜), or "maru", is a small circle at the upper right of a character. It is only used on the h-row, turning h→p.
kana.yoon_intro: Yoon combine a consonant+i kana (き, し, に, ...) with a small ya/yu/yo, read as a single syllable: きゃ is read "kya", not "ki-ya".
kana.yoon_dakuten_intro: The voiced form of the yoon above, using the dakuten/handakuten rows (が, じ, び, ぴ, etc.) as the consonant.

lampiran.title: Grammar Reference

lampiran.subtitle_n4: Pattern summaries and reference notes for N4, Lessons 1–25.
lampiran.n4_ndesu_forms_hint: Plain form + んです. Nouns and な-adjectives use な instead of だ.
lampiran.n4_trash_title: ごみの出し方 — How to Put Out Garbage
lampiran.n4_trash_subtitle: Types of household garbage and their collection days (general overview).
lampiran.n4_potential_forms_hint: Group I: final kana to the え row. Group II: 〜られる. Group III: irregular. The result conjugates like a group II verb.
lampiran.n4_shops_title: 近《ちか》くの店《みせ》 — Neighbourhood Shops
lampiran.n4_shops_subtitle: Services you usually find at repair shops, dry cleaners and convenience stores.
lampiran.n4_l3_patterns_hint: Five key patterns: ながら, habitual ています, し、し, それで, and とき + particles.
lampiran.n4_rental_title: うちを借りる — How to Read a Rental Listing
lampiran.n4_rental_subtitle: Terms that often appear in Japanese rental listings.
lampiran.section_n4_te_state: 〜て います & しまいます
lampiran.n4_te_verbs_hint: 〜て います describes the present state resulting from an event. The thing is marked with が.
lampiran.n4_te_compare_title: Two uses of 〜て います
lampiran.n4_shimau_title: Two functions of 〜て しまいます
lampiran.n4_condition_hint: Expressions for describing the state of things or people you can see in front of you.
lampiran.section_n4_teaoku: 〜て あります／おきます Summary
lampiran.n4_teaoku_compare: Comparing 〜て います, 〜て あります, 〜て おきます
lampiran.n4_teaoku_compare_hint: All three use the て-form, but they mean different things.
lampiran.n4_teaoku_pairs_hint: Intransitive for 〜て います (a state), transitive for 〜て あります (the result of an action).
lampiran.n4_bag_title: Inside an emergency bag (非常袋《ひじょうぶくろ》)
lampiran.n4_emergency_note: Evacuation sites and ways to reach family differ by area. Ask your local ward office for official information.
lampiran.n4_vol_forms_hint: The plain form of 〜ましょう. How you make it depends on the verb group.
lampiran.n4_vol_sounds_hint: The last sound of the dictionary form moves to the お-row, then う is added.
lampiran.n4_vol_uses: Patterns that use the volitional form, and intention/plan patterns
lampiran.n4_fields_subtitle: Names of academic fields, useful when talking about majors or specialities.
lampiran.n4_advice_title: Giving advice — 〜ほうが いいです
lampiran.n4_advice_hint: Vた to recommend doing, Vない to recommend not doing.
lampiran.n4_guess_title: Forming 〜でしょう／〜かもしれません
lampiran.n4_guess_hint: Plain form + でしょう／かもしれません. Nouns and な-adjectives are used without だ.
lampiran.n4_weather_hint: Expressions that often appear in weather forecasts.
lampiran.n4_regions_hint: The regional divisions used in forecasts, with example cities.
lampiran.n4_imp_forms_hint: Imperative: change by verb group. Prohibitive: dictionary form + な for every group.
lampiran.n4_imp_uses_hint: They sound strong, so use is limited. State verbs (ある, できる, わかる) have no imperative.
lampiran.n4_signs_subtitle: Writing and signs you meet in daily life (標識).
lampiran.section_n4_l9_summary: とおりに・あとで・ないで Summary
lampiran.n4_l9_forms_hint: た-form for とおりに／あとで, て-form for 〜て V, and ない-form + で.
lampiran.n4_l9_compare_title: あとで and てから
lampiran.n4_l9_compare_hint: Both mean "after", but the feel is different.
lampiran.n4_cond_hint: Verbs and い-adjectives use ば／ければ; な-adjectives and nouns use なら.
lampiran.n4_compare_hint: All mean "if/when", but the limits on the second part of the sentence differ.
lampiran.n4_proverbs_hint: Popular proverbs that make heavy use of the 〜ば form.
lampiran.n4_l11_patterns_hint: Five patterns: ように (purpose), ようになります, ようにしています／します, ようにしてください, and adjectives as adverbs.
lampiran.n4_adverb_hint: い → 〜く, な → 〜に. Exception: いい → よく.
lampiran.n4_health_bad: よくない習慣 — Habits that are not so good
lampiran.n4_nutrients_title: 5つの大切な栄養素 — Five important nutrients
lampiran.n4_nutrients_subtitle: Key nutrients and examples of foods that contain them.
lampiran.n4_passive_forms_hint: Group I: final kana to the あ row + れる. Group II: 〜られる. Group III: irregular. The result conjugates like a group II verb.
lampiran.n4_incidents_title: 事故《じこ》・事件《じけん》 — Accidents and Incidents
lampiran.n4_incidents_subtitle: Verbs that often appear in the news.
lampiran.n4_nominal_hint: Plain form + の turns the content of a sentence into something like a noun.
lampiran.n4_shiranai_title: 知《し》りません and 知《し》りませんでした
lampiran.n4_shiranai_hint: Two ways to answer "I do not know" to 〜を 知《し》って いますか.
lampiran.n4_position_hint: Expressions for saying where something is on a shelf, in a classroom, or on a page.
lampiran.n4_reason_hint: Comparing 〜て, Ｎで, 〜ので and 〜から. The back part of 〜て cannot express will.
lampiran.n4_node_hint: Plain form + ので. な-adjectives and nouns use な instead of だ.
lampiran.n4_tochuu_title: 途中で — on the way／in the middle of
lampiran.n4_feelings_hint: Feeling expressions that often form the back part of a 〜て sentence.
lampiran.n4_emb_forms_hint: Plain form + か. Nouns and な-adjectives lose だ. For yes/no questions add どうか.
lampiran.n4_measure_title: 単位・線・形・模様 — Units, Lines, Shapes, Patterns
lampiran.n4_measure_subtitle: Units of measurement, arithmetic words, lines, shapes and fabric patterns.
lampiran.n4_purpose_title: ために and ように — Stating Purpose
lampiran.n4_purpose_hint: Choose the pattern by the kind of verb and the target.
lampiran.n4_noni_hint: Dictionary-form verb + の, or noun + に, followed by a word that expresses use.
lampiran.n4_tools_title: 事務用品・道具 — Office Supplies & Tools
lampiran.n4_tools_hint: Everyday items for the office and workshop, with the verbs that go with them.
lampiran.n4_sou_forms_hint: Shows something about to happen (verbs) or an impression from appearance (adjectives): "it looks …".
lampiran.n4_char_title: 性格・性質 — Character and Traits
lampiran.n4_char_subtitle: Adjectives that describe a person's nature; opposite pairs are shown side by side.
lampiran.section_n4_l19_summary: すぎます・やすい・します Summary
lampiran.n4_l19_forms_hint: Drop ます, い, or な, then add the ending.
lampiran.n4_l19_change_title: なります and します
lampiran.n4_l19_change_hint: Changing by itself or being changed by someone.
lampiran.n4_salon_requests_hint: Combine with 〜 切って ください (please cut my hair).
lampiran.n4_giving_subtitle: Choose the word by the direction of giving and the standing of the people involved.
lampiran.n4_useful_hint: Terms from everyday ads and notices (便利情報) you often see in Japan.
lampiran.n4_baai_hint: 場合 is a noun, so it is attached the same way as any noun.
lampiran.n4_noni_compare_title: Comparing のに, が, ても
lampiran.n4_noni_compare_hint: All three express contrast, but their nuance and limits differ.
lampiran.section_n4_tokoro: ところ／ばかり／はずです
lampiran.n4_tokoro_title: ところです, ばかりです, はずです
lampiran.n4_tokoro_hint: The three points in time (before, during, after), the feeling of "recently", and a conclusion based on evidence.
lampiran.n4_hazu_hint: The word before はずです follows its own word type.
lampiran.n4_katakana_title: かたかな語《ご》のルーツ — Origins of Katakana Words
lampiran.n4_katakana_note: Besides loanwords, some katakana words were made in Japan from foreign words (for example アルバイト comes from German but its meaning has changed to a part-time job).
lampiran.section_n4_souyou: そうです／ようです Summary
lampiran.n4_souyou_hint: Comparing five expressions for news, impressions and guesses.
lampiran.n4_onomatope_title: 擬音語《ぎおんご》・擬態語《ぎたいご》 — Onomatopoeia
lampiran.n4_onomatope_hint: Words that imitate sounds and states, usually used with particular verbs.
lampiran.n4_caus_forms_hint: A causative verb conjugates like Group II (〜せます, 〜せる, 〜せない, 〜せて).
lampiran.n4_caus_endings_hint: Change the ending to the あ-row, then add せる.
lampiran.n4_discipline_title: しつける・鍛える — Raising & Discipline
lampiran.n4_discipline_hint: Things parents commonly make or let their children do, in causative sentences.
lampiran.n4_keigo_special_hint: The special form takes priority over the general patterns.
lampiran.n4_keigo_prefix_hint: Native Japanese words usually take お; words of Chinese origin usually take ご.
lampiran.n4_keigo_conj_hint: The ます-form ends in い, not り.
lampiran.n4_events_hint: Celebrations and customs that follow the seasons in Japan.
lampiran.n4_keigo_patterns_hint: Lowering your own action to respect the listener or the person the action is directed at.
lampiran.n4_keigo_verbs_hint: Special forms take priority over the お〜します pattern.
lampiran.n4_addr_title: 封筒・はがき — Addresses on Envelopes and Postcards
lampiran.n4_addr_subtitle: Where and how each part is written (vertically, from right to left).

home.rule_order: Sections are taken in order and can't be redone within one test.
home.rule_timer: Each section has a time limit. The clock runs on the server: closing the page or refreshing doesn't pause or reset it. When time runs out, your answers are submitted automatically.
home.rule_no_feedback: No right/wrong feedback during the exam. All scores appear in the recap once the test is finished.
home.rule_pass: You pass with a total of at least {n} and the minimum score in every part.
home.partial_notice: Only some sections are available so far. A provisional recap still appears after the available sections are done, but there is no pass/fail decision until every section exists.
home.abandon_body: All answers and sections in this test will be discarded, and you can start a new test from scratch.
home.mode_strict_hint: Exam conditions: each section is timed (on the server), audio plays once, and there is no right/wrong feedback during the test. Earns XP.
home.mode_practice_hint: No time limit. Each answer is marked right/wrong right away with an explanation, and listening audio can be replayed (original packs). Earns no XP.
home.rule_practice: Practice mode: feedback appears after you pick an answer, and you can change it.

jlptMock.title: JLPT Mock Test
jlptMock.subtitle: A full JLPT mock exam: 3 sections, time limits, audio that plays automatically, and an answer sheet — just like the real thing.
jlptMock.mode_strict_hint: Timed sections, audio plays once and automatically, you cannot go back to a finished section. Earns XP.
jlptMock.mode_practice_hint: No time limit, audio can be replayed and you continue manually. No XP.
jlptMock.furigana: Show furigana (not present in the real exam)
jlptMock.about_scoring: Scores here are estimates. The real JLPT uses equated scaled scores that cannot be computed from the number of correct answers alone, so raw counts are scaled linearly to the official ranges (language 0–120, listening 0–60). The N5 pass rule matches the real one: total at least 80, language at least 38, listening at least 19.
jlptMock.about_audio: Listening audio is generated with Google TTS, so it does not sound like the real exam recordings. Use headphones and find a quiet place.
jlptMock.load_error: Could not load the test. Please try again in a moment.
jlptMock.exit_body: Your answers are not saved and the test will be lost.
jlptMock.leave_confirm: A test is in progress. Leave now? Your answers will be lost.
jlptMock.time_up: Time ran out on the previous section. Answers you had marked still count.
jlptMock.rule_reading_1: Read each question on screen and choose the single best answer (1–4).
jlptMock.rule_reading_2: You can change answers any time until the time for this section is up. Open the Answer sheet to see unanswered questions.
jlptMock.rule_reading_3: Use the flag on questions you want to double-check.
jlptMock.rule_reading_timer: The {n}-minute timer starts when you press start. When it runs out the section is submitted automatically.
jlptMock.rule_listening_1: The audio contains instructions, an example, then numbered questions. Each question plays only once.
jlptMock.rule_listening_2: Choose your answer while the audio plays or during the answer pause. Once the next question starts, you cannot change it.
jlptMock.rule_listening_3_strict: Audio runs on its own until the end. There is no pause or replay button.
jlptMock.rule_listening_3_practice: Practice mode: audio can be replayed and you continue with the Next button.
jlptMock.rule_no_back: Once you submit this section you cannot return to it.
jlptMock.sheet_hint: Tap a number to jump to the question, or tap a bubble to mark an answer. Numbers outlined in yellow are unanswered.
jlptMock.finish_body: After submitting you cannot return to this section.

jlptMock.estimate_note: Estimated score — the real JLPT uses equated scaling.
jlptMock.practice_no_xp: Practice mode gives no XP. Try the real exam mode for XP.
